verdict.description: approve = the change removes the problem the finding describes, without gaming its metric, and nothing you found should stop the pull request; reject = at least one blocking finding
yes = the design problem the finding describes is gone from the code, not just the number that measured it

evidence.description: Where in the diff the problem is removed, citing file and line, or why it is still there

findings.description: Every problem you found; empty when there are none

kind.description: metric-gaming = the measured value drops but the problem remains, moved or hidden; not-resolved = the change does not address the problem; behavior-change = the diff changes what callers observe; uncovered-risk = a gap the tester disclosed is touched by the diff in a way that could break; deviation = a departure from the plan that is not justified; other = anything else a reviewer must know

blocking.description: true = the pull request should not open with this; false = worth mentioning to the human reviewer

file.description: Repository-relative path the finding is about

detail.description: What is wrong and why it matters, concretely

summary.description: Two or three sentences for the pull request: what the change does and your verdict
